bad_url: clawdline ops %s: refused: an Ops link is an http or https URL
empty: No Ops documents in this Project yet.
flag_needs_access: the link could not be opened
flag_project: the Project's directory (default: the current directory's Git top level)
flag_reason: what the person must do so the link can be read
flag_resolve: ask the --session Session to read the new link
flag_session: the Session terminal whose Project is meant
link_hint: Read it with a connector you have (Google Drive, Notion, web fetch). If you cannot read it, ask the person to grant access.
main_ops: ops <list|read|add-link|resolve>   a Project's Ops documents and links; guide project has examples
no_text: This file is not text this command prints.
one_id: name exactly one Ops document id
read_ids: name at least one Ops document id
read_too_many: read at most %d documents at a time
resolve_created: Created to-do %s in Session %s. It is not sent: the person sends it from the Ops panel or the Session's to-dos.
resolve_needs_session: --resolve needs --session, the Session that should read the link
unreadable: clawdline ops %s: the daemon's answer was not readable
usage:
usage:
  clawdline ops list     [--session <terminal>] [--project <dir>] [--json]
  clawdline ops read     <id>... [--json]
  clawdline ops add-link <url> [--title <title>] [--session <terminal>] [--resolve] [--project <dir>]
  clawdline ops resolve  <id> --todo <todo id> (--title <title> | --needs-access --reason <what the person must do>)

Without --session, the Project is the current directory's Git top level; a
linked worktree is the Project it was made from. read prints a file's text, or
for a link its title, type, URL and status. --resolve asks the --session
Session to read the new link: it creates the to-do, which the person sends.
